items.followUp: State four main postulates of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Identifies that electrons occupy allowed orbits with definite energies.
rubric.description: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in permitted orbits, each with a fixed energy.
rubric.how: Award for stating that electrons occupy permitted orbits with fixed energy.

rubric.why: States Bohr’s quantisation condition for an electron’s angular momentum.
rubric.description: The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantised: mvr = nh/2π.
rubric.how: Award for the correct quantisation equation or an equivalent expression.

rubric.why: States that electrons do not lose energy while remaining in an allowed orbit.
rubric.description: An electron does not radiate or lose energy while it remains in a permitted orbit.
rubric.how: Award for explicitly stating that an electron does not radiate energy in a permitted orbit.

rubric.why: Describes energy absorption and emission when an electron changes orbits.
rubric.description: An electron absorbs energy to move to a higher-energy orbit and emits energy when it moves to a lower-energy orbit; ΔE = hν.
rubric.how: Award for correctly linking absorption and emission to upward and downward transitions.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain permitted orbits, each having a fixed energy.
The angular momentum of an electron in an allowed orbit is quantised: mvr = nh/2π, where n is an integer.
An electron does not radiate or lose energy while it remains in a permitted orbit (stationary state).
An electron absorbs energy to move to a higher-energy orbit and emits energy when it moves to a lower-energy orbit; the energy change is ΔE = hν.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and explain its formation using sodium chloride as an example.

rubric.why: Identifies the pair of electrons involved in a coordinate covalent bond.
rubric.description: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond involving a shared pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a pair of electrons is shared.

rubric.why: Identifies that both shared electrons come from one atom.
rubric.description: The shared pair is donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award for stating that one atom provides or donates both electrons in the shared pair.

rubric.why: Gives a correct example of coordinate bond formation in ammonium ion.
rubric.description: NH₃ donates a lone pair to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺.
rubric.how: Award for the correct ammonia, hydrogen ion and ammonium ion example.

rubric.why: Gives a second correct example of coordinate bond formation in hydronium ion.
rubric.description: H₂O donates a lone pair to H⁺ to form H₃O⁺.
rubric.how: Award for the correct water, hydrogen ion and hydronium ion example.

rubric.why: Explains the donor–acceptor mechanism of coordinate bond formation.
rubric.description: One atom donates a lone pair to an electron-deficient atom or ion (the acceptor).
rubric.how: Award for identifying the lone-pair donor and the electron-deficient acceptor.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the shared pair of electrons is donated by one atom.
The donating atom supplies a lone pair to an electron-deficient atom or ion (the acceptor).
In ammonium ion formation, NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺; nitrogen in NH₃ donates its lone pair to H⁺.
In hydronium ion formation, H₂O + H⁺ → H₃O⁺; oxygen in H₂O donates its lone pair to H⁺.

items.followUp: What is an unsaturated solution? How can it be converted into a saturated solution?

rubric.why: States the defining maximum-solute condition for saturation.
rubric.description: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the solution contains the maximum amount of dissolved solute.

rubric.why: Specifies the solvent amount or temperature conditions for the definition.
rubric.description: The maximum amount dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a particular temperature.
rubric.how: Award for specifying the temperature or the amount of solvent.

rubric.why: Describes dissolving extra solute in a heated saturated solution.
rubric.description: Heat a saturated solution and dissolve additional solute in it.
rubric.how: Award for heating the solution and dissolving additional solute.

rubric.why: Describes the cooling step that produces a supersaturated solution.
rubric.description: Cool the solution slowly without disturbing it; the resulting solution is supersaturated.
rubric.how: Award for slow, undisturbed cooling and identifying the resulting solution as supersaturated.

modelAnswer: A saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent at a particular temperature.
Heat a saturated solution and dissolve additional solute in it.
Cool the solution slowly without disturbing it; the resulting solution is supersaturated.

items.followUp: Write two properties of proton particles.

rubric.description: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a neutron is electrically neutral.

rubric.description: A neutron has a mass of approximately 1 amu (1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg).
rubric.how: Award for either accepted approximate mass.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge.
Its mass is approximately 1 amu (1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg).
